description: Committee recommends declaring $26.7 million in land development profits.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Committee requested a report on increasing affordable housing allocation to 25%.
Administration clarified fund allocations are outside the regular budget process.

segments.title: Administration report on 2026 Land Development Fund profits
segments.takeaway: Administration presented a report recommending a $26.7 million dividend from the fund, allocating 10% to land acquisition, 15% to affordable housing, and 75% to major capital projects.

segments.title: Motion to increase affordable housing allocation for 2027
segments.takeaway: Councillor Ford moved to amend the policy to increase the allocation of net profits to the city's affordable housing program from 15% to 25% starting in 2027.

segments.title: Discussion and clarification on proposed policy change
segments.takeaway: Committee members discussed Councillor Ford's motion, clarifying its impact on discretionary funds and the possibility of rephrasing it as a request for a report on policy impacts.

segments.title: Vote on 2026 Land Development Fund profit allocation
segments.takeaway: The committee voted unanimously to approve the administration's recommendations for the 2026 Neighbourhood Land Development Fund profit allocation.

segments.title: Comments on report request for affordable housing allocation
segments.takeaway: Several councillors expressed concerns about the proposed policy change, arguing it bypasses the budget process and reduces flexibility in allocating funds.

segments.title: Procedural ruling on report request motion
segments.takeaway: The chair ruled that the motion was in order as a request for a report on policy impacts, which the committee could request directly.

segments.title: Vote on report request for affordable housing allocation
segments.takeaway: The committee voted to request a report from administration on the impacts of increasing the affordable housing program allocation from 15% to 25% for 2027 and onward.
